query:
In the spring season planning thread, who in the chat said something to the effect of 'an old C8 with about 6 hours of luminance is enough for a respectable galaxy result'?

Options:
A. Marcus
B. Tomas
C. Otis
D. Ravi
context:
[1] (about=Otis, episodic, t0 @2025-03-03T19:19:00) for what it's worth fellas, i shot M51 with my old C8 last april and got a pretty decent result. 6 hours of luminance, that's all you really need.
[2] (about=Diego, episodic, t0 @2025-03-03T19:20:00) luminance is king for galaxies imo. wavelets do nothing on faint extended structure
[3] (about=Marcus, episodic, t17 @2025-05-05T20:10:00) spring galaxy season is winding down. Summer is narrowband and milky way territory. What is the group's plan?
[4] (about=Yara, episodic, t10 @2025-04-07T11:42:00) okay separately from marcus's solar thing, I want to share something. I've been only doing messier objects but I tried the integrated flux nebula in cygnus last weekend with 12 hours of luminance and got something visible 🤔
[5] (about=Marcus, episodic, t4 @2025-03-17T20:27:00) narrowband through city skies works. pure RGB galaxies through city skies, less so.
[6] (about=Diego, episodic, t2 @2025-03-10T19:08:00) jupiter still high enough at 8pm. got 200 frames on the GRS friday, seeing was a 4/10 but barely usable
[7] (about=Bex, episodic, t4 @2025-03-17T20:12:00) no way. portability is the whole point. I'd rather drive 90min with a redcat than 6 hours with a c8
[8] (about=Diego, episodic, t4 @2025-03-17T20:29:00) planetary couldn't care less about light pollution btw. atmospheric seeing is the only thing that matters imo
[9] (about=Bex, episodic, t10 @2025-04-07T11:56:00) luc post a milky way pano from singapore for us 🚗
[10] (about=Nia, episodic, t16 @2025-04-28T10:04:00) first dark site!! the milky way naked eye is genuinely a different thing than I expected ✨ literally couldn't believe it

query:
After the group discussed how cloud cancellations had reshaped a member's site choice, who said something to the effect that good-enough conditions every night beat perfect conditions a few times a year?

Options:
A. Bex
B. Camila
C. Henrik
D. Marcus
context:
[1] (about=Camila, episodic, t4 @2025-03-17T20:15:00) ymmv but the desert teaches you that good-enough conditions every night beats perfect conditions twice a year
[2] (about=Camila, episodic, t4 @2025-03-17T20:14:00) honestly Bex this resonates with me. every clear-sky chase I've made cost more than it gave back
[3] (about=Ravi, episodic, t4 @2025-03-17T20:09:00) Frankly: the obsession with bortle 1 has always been performative for most members of this hobby. Bortle 3 with a clear sky beats Bortle 1 under cirrus every time.
[4] (about=Marcus, episodic, t4 @2025-03-17T20:07:00) the math always favored closer dark sites anyway. the Bortle 1 vs 3 SNR delta is small once you control for travel-stress and setup quality.
[5] (about=Henrik, episodic, t4 @2025-03-17T20:20:00) There's a signal-to-noise argument here as well. Per unit clear sky time, a regular Bortle 3 with 50 sessions a year integrates more useful photons than a Bortle 1 you reach four times per year. The math favors consistency.
[6] (about=Priya, episodic, t4 @2025-03-17T20:17:00) fwiw I lurk on the cherry springs facebook group and the fall trips have like 60% cloud cancellation rate. tbh
[7] (about=Aida, episodic, t2 @2025-03-10T19:17:00) Good. The dust shadow problem from last spring was preventable. I think more members should adopt this.
[8] (about=Tomas, episodic, t10 @2025-04-07T11:32:00) Marcus, that opens up daytime sessions. You'll never have a clouded-out morning the way you do at night. Frankly this is going to consume your weekends.
[9] (about=Theo, episodic, t4 @2025-03-17T20:05:00) Bex, that's a really sensible adjustment. Two clouded weekends in a row is enough data to update on, in my experience.
[10] (about=Ravi, episodic, t16 @2025-04-28T10:44:00) the trip-goers seem to have had a good time. I will note that backyard sessions do not produce post-trip exhaustion. point taken on the social value.
